questions.question: Which two questions choose the journal for any transaction?
options: Did money move, and in which direction — and if not, what happened?
Is it recurring, and is it material?
Is it an asset or an expense?

questions.question: R2 400 collected from a debtor is recorded in:
options: The DJ, next to the original sale
The General Journal with a narration
The CRJ's Debtors Control column, plus the debtor's page — never Sales

questions.question: Paying a creditor on account never touches Trading Stock because:
options: Trading Stock only changes at year end
The payment settles the debt; the stock was recorded via the CJ on delivery day
Creditors are recorded in the Debtors Ledger

questions.question: An irrecoverable debt is written off through the:
options: General Journal — no money and no goods moved

questions.question: The credit sale to T. Mokoena (R4 500, mark-up 50% on cost) writes in the DJ:
options: Sales R4 500 and Cost of Sales R3 000
Sales R4 500 and Cost of Sales R2 250

questions.question: Mokoena appears in three different journals during the month because:
options: A single customer can generate a sale (DJ), a return (DAJ) and a receipt (CRJ) — his page collects all three
Every debtor must appear in every journal

questions.question: Returning R1 000 of damaged stock to Bayside Suppliers is recorded in the:
options: CAJ, with Bayside's page debited and a numbered debit note issued

subtopics.title: Posting the Month and Proving It

questions.question: Bank's closing balance (R41 400 in, R13 200 out) is:
Debtors Control closes at R1 200 debit, and this must equal:
options: The debtors list — Mokoena R1 200, Khumalo closed

questions.question: The month's trial balance levels at:
In equation terms, Mokoena's R2 400 payment was:
options: A swap inside A — Bank up, Debtors Control down

subtopics.title: The Control Web Around the Month

questions.question: Under the perpetual system, the R2 600 Trading Stock balance is a 'claim' because:
options: The supplier can reclaim unsold goods
A physical count can test it — any shortage now has an exact size
It is only an estimate of value
It belongs to the owner personally

questions.question: Khumalo's write-off was ethically sound because:
options: The owner was tired of him
It followed documented, dated follow-up and carries a narration — prudence acting on evidence

questions.question: Bayside's invoice was recorded only after:
options: The order, delivery note and invoice were matched and told one story

questions.question: Mokoena's R2 400 goes through the money-in door but is NOT a sale because:
options: His sale went through the trust door on the 9th; this paper only shrinks what his page says he owes
It was paid in cash rather than by card
The amount is below the sales threshold

questions.question: The paper that slips through the odd-jobs door is:
options: The letter confirming Khumalo will never pay — no money, no goods, one explaining sentence

questions.question: The sorting goes quickly because:
options: It is two questions asked eleven times, not eleven procedures memorised
The doors are labelled by amount
There are only two kinds of paper
The journals sort themselves at month end

questions.question: Mokoena's page at month end reads:
The stock account's R2 600 balance means:
options: R2 600 of goods was sold this month
Goods costing R2 600 should be standing on the shelf, checkable by counting
R2 600 is still owed to Bayside

questions.question: The level weigh-in at R47 900 certifies that:
options: The bank statement agrees with the till
Eleven events crossed six journals and two ledgers with no rand lost or invented

questions.question: Stop two of the Friday walk checks:
options: A sample of shelf lines counted against the stock account's claim

questions.question: Khumalo's R400 is the walk's cautionary tale because it teaches that:
options: Debts age badly — the debtors list must be read weekly, not discovered at write-off
Letters are stronger than phone calls

questions.question: The whole walk is only possible because:
options: The shop is small enough to see at a glance
The owner has an excellent memory
The books give every question a record to check against
